 Taoyuan International Airport. CNA file photo 
 Taipei, Oct. 21 (CNA) China Airlines and Tigerair Taiwan Wednesday announced changes to Thursday flights between Taiwan and Okinawa as Typhoon Champi approaches, while two domestic carriers canceled some flights and other airlines said their services were unchanged.
 China Airlines said Thursday's flights CI122/CI123 between Taoyuan and Okinawa, CI312/CI313 between Taichung and Okinawa and CI132/CI133 between Kaohsiung and Okinawa had been canceled, while CI310/CI311 between Taichung and Okinawa would depart earlier.
 The airline said it would continue to update flight information based on the typhoon's track and advised passengers to check its website or mobile app for the latest updates.
 An aircraft of Tigerair Taiwan. CNA file photo Tigerair Taiwan said it had canceled Thursday's flights IT232/IT233 between Taoyuan and Okinawa, IT289/IT728 between Kaohsiung and Okinawa, IT793 from Okinawa to Taichung and IT796 from Tainan to Okinawa, and advised passengers to check its website or mobile app for the latest information.
 Starlux Airlines said no flights had been changed as of Wednesday but warned that some flights in the coming days could be affected by the weather. It advised passengers to check its website and watch for updates sent by email or text message.
 EVA Air said its flights remained unchanged but warned that some Taiwan-Japan services could be affected in the coming days. It urged passengers to check their flight status before going to the airport and to visit its website for ticket change and refund information.
 Among domestic carriers, Uni Air said flights from Taiwan proper to Penghu after 10 a.m. Thursday would be canceled, as would flights between Taichung and Matsu and between Taichung and Kinmen after 11:30 a.m. Other flights were expected to operate normally, though some schedules could change, the airline said.
 Mandarin Airlines said some Thursday flights on its Songshan-Kinmen, Songshan-Penghu, Taichung-Kinmen, Taichung-Penghu and Kaohsiung-Penghu routes would be canceled, and that it would adjust other flights based on weather conditions.
 As of 2 p.m. Wednesday, Champi was centered about 910 kilometers east-southeast of Eluanbi, Taiwan's southernmost point, moving northwest at 19 kilometers per hour, the Central Weather Administration said.
 (By Yu Hsiao-han and Shih Hsiu-chuan)
